This notebook looks for common sources of error and flags those records manual revision by the assessors who capture data from each country. ACK adapted this from the original Gingko code.

The output are:
* a report of the quality check
* A .csv file (called ´kobo_output_tocheck.csv´) showing **the records that need manual review or corrections**, if any.
* A .csv file (called ´kobo_output_clean.csv´) with the data after processing (**records flagged in the previous file may or may not be included according to user choice**).

## Libraries and functions

Load required libraries:

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(utile.tools)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
```

Useful custom functions

```{r}
# "Not in" function
"%!in%" <- function(x, y)!('%in%'(x,y))
```

## Variables that need to be set by the user

Output from KoboToolbox in .csv format as downloaded using [these instructions](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/5_Data_collection/Kobo_toolbox_help.html). 

```{r}
kobo_file="koboForms/NATTIC_KOBO_2026-11-13.csv"
```
Should records that need manual review and potentially correction be removed or kept in the exported "clean" data?. True to keep, false to filter them. Defaults to FALSE
```{r}
keep_to_check=TRUE #true to keep, false to filter them. 
```

## Get data
Get Kobo raw output data:
```{r, results='hide'}
# kobo_file variable is defined at the start of this script; it should be csv file
kobo_output<-read.csv(file=kobo_file, sep=";", header=TRUE) %>%

# Add  taxon column, which is a combination of genus and species names
mutate(taxon=(utile.tools::paste(genus, species, subspecies_variety, na.rm=TRUE))) %>%
    # remove white space at the end of the name
    mutate(taxon=str_trim(taxon, "right"))
```
Filter out records which were marked as "not_approved" in the manual Kobo validation interface (this means country assessors determined the is something wrong with that particular record).

NOTE: These lines are leading to the loss of all data in the `kobo_output` object--so, commenting out for now.
```{r}
# # check if any species is flagged as "validation_status_not_approved"
# kobo_output %>%
#       filter(X_validation_status=="validation_status_not_approved")  %>%
#             select(country_assessment, name_assessor, taxon)
# 
# # omit those records from data:
# kobo_output<- kobo_output %>%
#             filter(X_validation_status!="validation_status_not_approved")
```

### Filter out any sort of tests
```{r, results='hide'}
# Select likely columns to say "test"
cols= c("name_assessor", "email_assessor", "genus", "species", "subspecies_variety",
         "scientific_authority", "common_name", "GBIF_taxonID", "NCBI_taxonID")

# Check for "test" or "template" in any of the selected columns
kobo_output %>% 
  filter(if_any(all_of(cols), ~ grepl("test", .)) |
         if_any(all_of(cols), ~ grepl("Template", .)))  %>% 
  select(country_assessment, name_assessor, genus, species)

# Filter them out of dataset
kobo_output<- kobo_output %>% 
              filter(if_any(all_of(cols), ~ !grepl("test", .))) %>% 
              filter(genus!="Template")
```

### Filter out species no longer included in final species list
These species were assessed early on in the project, but we ultimately decided to not include them.
```{r, results='hide'}
# Specify excluded taxa
excludedTaxa <- 
  c("Betula murrayana", "Conocarpus erectus", "Guaiacum officinale",
    "Mespilus canescens", "Mosiera longipes", "Pteralyxia kauaiensis",
    "Quercus graciliformis", "Zanthoxylum fagara")
# Filter these out of the dataset
kobo_output <- kobo_output %>% 
  filter(!taxon %in% excludedTaxa)
```

### Filter out additional Torreya taxifolia submission
Torreya taxifolia was assessed twice, but not as a multi-assessment. The assessment from Roberta needs to removed prior to processing.
```{r, results='hide'}
# Find which rows Torreya taxifolia is found in
which(kobo_output$taxon == "Torreya taxifolia")[[1]]
kobo_output$name_assessor[which(kobo_output$taxon == "Torreya taxifolia")]
# Remove Torreya taxifolia submission from Roberta
kobo_output <- 
  kobo_output[-which(kobo_output$taxon == "Torreya taxifolia")[[1]],]
```

## Check for common data capture errors

### Number of populations
In the form, -999 was used to mark taxa with unknown number of extant or extinct populations. This was used because answering the question was mandatory, so leaving it blank wasn't possible. 
The first change to make is to see if anyone mistyped -999, for these fields. We check any values over 900.

```{r, results='hide'}
# Correct extant populations
kobo_output <- kobo_output %>%
  mutate(n_extant_populations = if_else(n_extant_populations > 900, -999, n_extant_populations))
# Correct extinct populations
kobo_output <- kobo_output %>%
  mutate(n_extinct_populations = if_else(n_extinct_populations > 900, -999, n_extinct_populations))
```

Next, we have to change all -999 instances to NA.
```{r, results='hide'}
kobo_output<-kobo_output %>%
             mutate(n_extant_populations= na_if(n_extant_populations, -999))
kobo_output<-kobo_output %>%
             mutate(n_extinct_populations= na_if(n_extinct_populations, -999))
```

We can now explore how many populations per species are still extant 
```{r, results='hide'}
summary(kobo_output$n_extant_populations)
table(kobo_output$n_extant_populations)
```

Plot histogram
```{r, results='hide'}
ggplot(kobo_output, aes(x=n_extant_populations))+
      geom_histogram()
```

Zoom Plot histogram
```{r, results='hide'}
kobo_output %>%
    filter(n_extant_populations>=0, n_extant_populations<25) %>%

ggplot(., aes(x=n_extant_populations))+
      geom_histogram()
```

Once -999 was replaced by NA there should be no negative number of populations (if they are, they are typos that need to be corrected).
```{r, results='hide'}
kobo_output %>%
      filter(n_extant_populations<0) %>%
      select(country_assessment, taxon, name_assessor, n_extant_populations, n_extinct_populations)
```

Show which taxa (if any) have 0 (zero) extant populations. **Is this correct? needs to be manually checked**
```{r, results='hide'}
kobo_output %>%
      filter(n_extant_populations==0) %>%
      select(country_assessment, taxon, name_assessor, n_extant_populations, n_extinct_populations)
```

Show which species (if any) have 999 extant populations. **Should this be -999? OR n_extinct pops??**
```{r, results='hide'}
kobo_output %>%
      filter(n_extant_populations==999) %>%
      select(country_assessment, taxon, name_assessor, n_extant_populations, n_extinct_populations)
```

Show which species (if any) have 999 EXTINCT populations. **Should this be -999?**
```{r, results='hide'}
kobo_output %>%
      filter(n_extinct_populations==999) %>%
      select(country_assessment, taxon, name_assessor, n_extant_populations, n_extinct_populations)
```
Put all taxa with weird number of populations that need to be checked together:

```{r, results='hide'}
check_n_pops <- kobo_output %>% 
      # variables of interest
      select(country_assessment, name_assessor, taxon, n_extant_populations, n_extinct_populations) %>%

      # same filters that discussed above
      filter(n_extant_populations<0 |
            n_extant_populations==0 | 
            n_extant_populations==999 | 
            n_extinct_populations==999) %>% 

# add a column stating what needs to be checked:
       mutate(need_to_check="check number of extant or extint populations. Are 0 correct? should 999 be -999? are extant/extint confused?")
```

### Idiosyncratic issues
#### Chamaecyparis thyoides
There were three submissions of this species, when there only need to be two. After removing the third, we also need to correct the EOO value in one of the two remaining submissions, so that the EOOs match between the two submissions.
```{r, results='hide'}
# Remove data.frame row of species with 3 separate submissions
kobo_output <- 
  kobo_output %>% slice(-which(kobo_output$taxon == "Chamaecyparis thyoides - 2"))
# Match EOOs between remaining Chamaecyparis thyoides submissions
kobo_output$occurrence_extent[which(kobo_output$taxon == "Chamaecyparis thyoides")]
# Correct the second value, to match the first value
kobo_output$occurrence_extent[which(kobo_output$taxon == "Chamaecyparis thyoides")][[2]] <- kobo_output$occurrence_extent[which(kobo_output$taxon == "Chamaecyparis thyoides")][[1]]
```

#### Quercus pacifica
This KOBO submission has 0 extant populations, but according to the assessor, this is a mistake; the appropriate number of extant populations is 1. We correct this.
```{r, results='hide'}
# Report original number of extant populations for Quercus pacifica
kobo_output$n_extant_populations[[which(kobo_output$taxon == "Quercus pacifica")]]
# Correct number of extant populations
kobo_output$n_extant_populations[[which(kobo_output$taxon == "Quercus pacifica")]] <- 1
```

### Species names

Genus, species and subspecies should be a single word, check if there are cases where it isn't. Only exception would be "var." or "subsp." in the subspecies_variety field: 

```{r, results='hide'}
kobo_output %>% 
  filter(grepl(" ", genus) | 
         grepl(" ", species) | 
         grepl(" ", subspecies_variety)) %>%
   filter(!grepl("var.", subspecies_variety)) %>%
   filter(!grepl("subsp.", subspecies_variety)) %>%
  # show only relevant columns
            select(country_assessment, name_assessor, taxon, genus, species, subspecies_variety)
```
Put them in their own happy df with a column stating what is the likely problem:

```{r, results='hide'}
check_taxon_names <- kobo_output %>% 
  filter(grepl(" ", genus) | 
         grepl(" ", species) | 
         grepl(" ", subspecies_variety)) %>%
   filter(!grepl("var.", subspecies_variety)) %>%
   filter(!grepl("subsp.", subspecies_variety)) %>%
  # show only relevant columns
            select(country_assessment, name_assessor, taxon, genus, species, subspecies_variety) %>%
       mutate(need_to_check="check genus, species or subspecies_variety, we are targeting to have single words in each field, except in the ifraspecific names, where 'var.' and 'subsp.' (only) would be accepted. Other details or taxonomic notes should be added in the comments.")
```

## Create a single file for assessors review:

```{r, results='hide'}
to_check<-full_join(check_n_pops, check_GBIF) %>% full_join(check_taxon_names) %>%
  # show columns in desired order:
select(country_assessment, name_assessor, taxon, need_to_check, n_extant_populations,
         n_extinct_populations, GBIF_taxonID, genus, species, subspecies_variety)

# save file:
write.csv(to_check, "kobo_output_tocheck.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
```

## Save the clean koboutput version, removing any taxa with issues:

Asks the user if they want to keep the taxa flagged in the previous step, or if they should be filtered out.

```{r, results='hide'}
# keep_to_check variable is defined at the start of the script. It should be TRUE/FALSE
if(keep_to_check==FALSE){
# Remove from the clean version any remaining taxa with issues
kobo_clean<-kobo_output %>%
            filter(taxon %!in% to_check$taxon)
print(paste("A total of", nrow(to_check), "records were excluded from the cleaned data"))
# Export clean version
write.csv(kobo_clean, "kobo_output_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
} else {
write.csv(kobo_output, "kobo_output.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
}
```
